content.user_title: Build Therapeutic ML Workflows with PyTDC
content.value_statement: Therapeutic machine learning requires reliable datasets, meaningful splits, and consistent evaluation. This skill guides PyTDC workflows from dataset selection through molecular optimization.
actual_capabilities: Selects PyTDC task classes and datasets for ADME, toxicity, interaction, and generation workflows.
Explains scaffold, random, temporal, and cold split strategies for realistic model evaluation.
Provides five-seed benchmark guidance with PyTDC evaluators and leaderboard-compatible summaries.
Demonstrates molecular oracle scoring, batch evaluation, multi-objective weighting, and constraint checks.
Documents molecule conversion, filtering, balancing, negative sampling, and biomedical identifier retrieval utilities.
limitations: Requires PyTDC and optional scientific dependencies that may need separate installation.
Dataset loading and some oracles may download resources or require external API access.
Example scripts use simulated predictions and do not provide a trained machine learning model.
Oracle scores are computational estimates and cannot replace experimental or clinical validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare ADMET Experiments
use_cases.description: Choose property datasets, create scaffold splits, and select evaluation metrics for reproducible molecular prediction studies.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Interaction Models
use_cases.description: Evaluate drug-target or drug-drug models with cold splits, multiple seeds, and standardized PyTDC metrics.

use_cases.title: Screen Generated Molecules
use_cases.description: Score candidate molecules with property oracles and compare candidates against multi-objective constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Load an ADME Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a PyTDC ADME dataset for [property]. Explain its columns, task type, scaffold split, and suitable evaluation metric.

prompt_templates.title: Design a DTI Split
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PyTDC drug-target interaction experiment using [dataset]. Compare random, cold-drug, and cold-target splits, then recommend one.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Benchmark Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a five-seed PyTDC benchmark for [dataset group] and [model]. Include predictions, evaluation, aggregation, and reproducibility checks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Molecular Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-objective molecular workflow using [oracles]. Define score normalization, weights, constraints, diversity checks, and experimental validation steps.

output_examples.input: Recommend a dataset and split for predicting intestinal permeability.
output_examples.output: Use Caco2_Wang from the ADME task. Apply a scaffold split and evaluate regression performance with MAE across several seeds.

output_examples.input: How should I test generalization to unseen drugs in BindingDB_Kd?
output_examples.output: Use a cold-drug split. Confirm that drug identifiers do not overlap between training and test partitions before fitting the model.

output_examples.input: Outline a balanced molecular scoring workflow using QED, SA, GSK3B, and LogP.
output: Normalize every oracle to a comparable direction and range.
Set weights and acceptable property intervals before scoring candidates.
Retain diverse candidates and validate top results experimentally.

best_practices: Use scaffold or cold splits when random splits would overstate real-world generalization.
Run multiple fixed seeds and report both mean performance and variability.
Validate dataset names, metrics, oracle ranges, and optional dependencies before large experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not treat simulated predictions in the example scripts as model baselines.
Do not compare models that use different splits, seeds, preprocessing, or metrics.
Do not interpret oracle scores as experimental evidence or clinical recommendations.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers PyTDC datasets, splits, evaluators, benchmark groups, utilities, generation tasks, and molecular oracles.

faq.question: Does the skill train a model?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow templates and evaluation guidance, while you supply and train the model.

faq.question: Which split should I use for molecular property prediction?
faq.answer: Use a scaffold split when you need performance estimates across chemically distinct structures.

faq.question: How should I evaluate drug-target interaction models?
faq.answer: Choose cold-drug or cold-target splits when the deployment setting includes unseen entities.

faq.question: Does PyTDC require internet access?
faq.answer: Initial dataset loading may download data, and selected oracles may require external resources or APIs.

faq.question: Are molecular oracle results suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. Oracle scores are computational estimates that require experimental and clinical validation.
